To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the supply of SRP to virally infected M. pusilla stimulated virus production far into the infection cycle, 2) P-limited M.pusilla utilized several different P sources with the same efficiency, and 3) virus-free lysate enhanced virus production.
virus proliferation in P-limited Micomonas pusilla is stimulated by a supply (mimicking remineralization) of low concentrations of different P sources, far into its lytic cycle.
the supply of P, regardless of the source, stimulates virus proliferation in P-limited M.pusilla, far into the viral lytic cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how the supply of naturally occurring SNP concentrations to P-limited M.pusilla stimulates MpV production, which is of importance to the ecology of marine viruses and their role in biogeochemical cycles.
the importance of SNP utilization by P-limited hosts for the proliferation of viruses in the environment, and how this can be stimulated by low concentrations of different P sources.
how the supply of P, and in particular the source of P (i.e. SRP or SNP), can affect viral production and the subsequent fate of infected cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the addition of low P concentrations to P-limited M.pusilla stimulated virus production by the supply of both SRP and SNP, far into the infection cycle, and that host-associated alkaline-phosphatase activity was important in this process.
the supply of P, in the form of both SRP and SNP, stimulates the proliferation of viruses in P-limited phytoplankton.
virus proliferation is stimulated by the supply of P, regardless of its source.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
virus proliferation in natural marine waters can be stimulated through the addition of a low concentration of any P source.
the proliferation of viruses in P-limited phytoplankton is not limited by P starvation but rather by the availability of P sources.
the proliferation of viruses can be stimulated by P supply, even far into the lytical cycle, and this stimulation may be independent of the P source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proliferation of viruses in P-limited hosts is stimulated by a steady supply of low P concentrations, regardless of the P source.
P-limited M.pusilla can efficiently use SNP, even when the host cells have already started to produce viruses.
P limitation of M. pusilla does not prevent the proliferation of viruses.
